items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: Well, I don't know, Papa Lee, but he didn't play... But I think Papa Lane played jazz in the parades that he played.

ctx.x: Was that the first time, to your knowledge, that anybody had made those renovations?

Well, I don't know, Papa Lee, but he didn't play. You see, he wasn't union. He was non-union at that time. And he didn't play in the Rex Parade. The Rex Parade was the only parade that used a union band, and always did, you see. But I think Papa Lane played jazz in the parades that he played. But I don't know whether they did that thing with the drum thing, like we did, you know, played the jazz.
Back in those days, did your father and the other people who were playing that kind of music think of themselves as jazz musicians, as doing something different?

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, before I forget, you mentioned that, uh, word double drums. I've heard Papa Lane talk about that. Just what do you mean?

ctx.x: Well, when I first started, yes. Because, uh, another little story about Rag Baby. Uh, incidentally, he has a son who works in the quarter. Yeah. Yeah. Nah. Well, Rag Baby was, uh, he always had, uh, lady troubles. And, uh, he, he was, uh, he, he left his family. I think he had six, seven kids, something like that. And he left to pull out on the family. And the, the police were always hounding him, you know, for alimony. And, uh, my dad would have to carry me along because they, they had places like the Southern…
Well, before I forget, you mentioned that, uh, word double drums. I've heard Papa Lane talk about that. Just what do you mean?

Well, instead of having one man play both drums, you know, with the foot pedal and that, well, you had, you had two men. One played the bass drum and one played the snare drum. Not only in parades, now this was for any, any, any dances at all. Because there was no such thing as the foot pedal there.
